lines: In your own words, what's weighing on you right now? No need to be organized.
It sounds like work has been relentless and nights go to replaying meetings, with one part of you saying push harder and another wanting to hide under the covers.
Which feeling has been loudest lately — what would you call it?
Thank you for giving it a name.
And how do you feel toward ‘not feeling good enough’ — curious about it, frustrated with it, or something else?
It sounds like you feel frustrated with 'not feeling good enough' right now.
There may be another feeling here too.
If it feels separate, what would you call it — or is it part of the same feeling?
It sounds like "the one who wants to hide" feels like its own part, separate from the part that says to push harder.
Which feels closer — ‘not feeling good enough’ or ‘the one who wants to hide’?
It sounds like the part of you that wants to hide under the covers feels closer right now, the one that doesn't want to deal with any of it.

One way I'm seeing this is that ‘not feeling good enough’ takes up the most space; ‘the one who wants to hide’ feels closer than ‘not feeling good enough’; and the two seem to be pulling in different directions — what would you change?
That sounds like how you'd like it to be — you could try that in ‘What if’.
That's the picture so far — it's yours. Move anything that doesn't look right.
What would you call the part that rarely gets heard?
‘the tired one’ is here now, at the edge. Move it wherever feels right.
If ‘not feeling good enough’ had words, what would it say?
It sounds like 'not feeling good enough' tells you that you can't stop now, or everything falls apart.
What might ‘not feeling good enough’ be trying to do for you?
It sounds like 'not feeling good enough' might be trying to keep you from being let go, telling you that you can't stop now.
The map now shows that ‘not feeling good enough’ feels about as close as ‘the one who wants to hide’. Is anything different about it?
It sounds like, with 'not feeling good enough' about as close as 'the one who wants to hide,' things feel a bit quieter over there.
In your words: ‘I wish it were further away.’ Would it be alright to try that here, and notice what shifts? Undo is one tap.
What was that like?
It sounds like with 'the one who wants to hide' sitting further out, things felt lighter, like there was more room to breathe.
‘How it is’ hasn't changed — both pictures are here.

timeline.note: One way I'm seeing this is that ‘not feeling good enough’ takes up the most space and feels about as close as ‘the one who wants to hide’; the two seem to be pulling in different directions; and ‘the tired one’ rarely gets heard.
